assertions.text: Package options (fragile, insuredValue, handling) are collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500] — not kept as three separate columns with mostly-blank cells. Rows with no options use a blank cell or [:].
assertions.evidence: Options are passed as individual boolean/String parameters (fragile, handling, insuredValue) in table columns, not as a collapsed map like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500].

assertions.text: A @TypeConverter method is present that accepts Map<String, String> (or similar) and returns PackageOptions, applying defaults for missing keys.
assertions.evidence: No @TypeConverter method is present in the test file. Options are constructed manually in test methods.

assertions.text: Dimensions are represented as a [L, W, H] list in the table — not as three separate length/width/height columns
assertions.evidence: Dimensions appear as List<Integer> columns: 'Dimensions | [10, 10, 10]' and 'Dimensions | [70, 50, 10]'

assertions.text: At least one table uses value set syntax {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} (or subset) to express carrier equivalence, rather than duplicating rows per carrier
Multiple @TableTest methods exist, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing base rates, surcharges, dimensional weight, and carrier equivalence
assertions.evidence: 8 separate @TableTest methods: calculatesBaseRateByZoneAndWeight, appliesDimensionalWeightWhenGreaterThanActual, appliesOversizeSurchargeWhenAnyDimensionExceedsLimit, appliesFragileSurcharge, appliesInsurancePremiumWithMinimum, appliesHazmatHandlingFee, combinesSurchargesInOrder, carrierDoesNotAffectPrice

assertions.text: Parameter types correspond to the ShippingCostCalculator.calculateShippingCost interface — weight, cost, and dimension types match the method signature.
assertions.evidence: Weight is double, cost is BigDecimal, dimensions are List<Integer>: 'calculator.calculateShippingCost(zone, weight, DEFAULT_DIMENSIONS, new PackageOptions(), Carrier.DHL)'

assertions.text: Each table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
Scenario names describe conditions ('EU express, light package', 'Oversized with fragile') — not outcomes ('8.00', 'Surcharge applied') or generic labels ('Test 1').
assertions.evidence: Scenario names describe conditions: 'EU standard, light', 'EU express, medium', 'Large package, dimensional weight used', 'Just over the limit', 'Fragile surcharge applied'

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Cost?', 'Base rate?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Base Rate?, Rate?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?

assertions.text: Column names use domain language ('Zone', 'Weight (kg)', 'Dimensions', 'Options', 'Cost?') — not code identifiers ('shippingZone', 'weightKg', 'dims')
assertions.evidence: Column headers use business language: 'Region', 'Speed', 'Weight', 'Base Rate?', 'Dimensions', 'Total Cost?', 'Fragile', 'Handling', 'Insured Value', 'Carrier'
